constraints: requires crushing on-site or nearby facility
concrete.notes: Crush and reuse as road base or new concrete aggregate

constraints: treated wood cannot be reused directly
wood.notes: Reuse if untreated; downcycle to mulch/particleboard if treated

drywall.notes: Gypsum can be reprocessed into new drywall or used as soil amendment

asphalt.notes: Reclaimed asphalt pavement (RAP) is widely reused in new asphalt mixes

constraints: intact bricks can be reused; broken brick is downcycled as fill
brick.notes: Whole bricks have high reuse value; rubble becomes aggregate fill

constraints: contamination from other materials lowers value
glass.notes: Clean glass can be recycled into new glass products or glasphalt

plastic.notes: Construction plastics (PVC piping, sheeting) recyclable if sorted by resin type

insulation.notes: Often landfilled; some fiberglass/foam programs exist regionally

constraints: requires manual or mechanical sorting before any recovery is possible
mixed_debris.notes: Default fallback when materials cannot be cleanly separated; recommend sorting
